title: An inventor’s portfolio
question: Choose the world for your homepage. All project material will be explicitly marked as placeholder until you replace it.

options.label: The Future Institute
options.lineage: Experimental research-institute identity and spatial exhibition graphics
options.thesis: Your engineering practice becomes a vivid, navigable research exhibition rather than a fictional control panel.
options.viewport: A cobalt field holds one oversized illustrative mechanism, a large inventor statement, and an integrated vertical work index; the next exhibit begins at the bottom edge.
options.risk: More visionary research institute than cinematic workshop; placeholder imagery must not masquerade as your actual engineering work.

raised.raise: Direct access to every work entry without making visitors play through an introduction.
One shared interaction changes the complete illustrative mechanism rather than adding isolated hover tricks.
Every displayed project can trace from overview to your role and supporting evidence.
Render objects with convincing material variation rather than sterile stock geometry.
The opening owns the whole viewport with a single memorable focal object.
One repeatable structural grammar connects the homepage, future case studies, and T labs.

options.label: The Inventor’s Workshop
options.lineage: Optical laboratories and precision prototype demonstrations
options.thesis: An inspectable object fills the opening, making the connection between physical engineering and intelligence tangible.
options.viewport: A large illustrated prototype occupies the center, your introduction anchors the lower left, and a narrow project selector runs across the bottom.
options.risk: Closest to the familiar cinematic inventor aesthetic; avoid neon HUD decoration and invented technical readings.

options.label: Engineering Broadcast
options.thesis: Projects become directly addressable pages in a block-mosaic engineering broadcast.
options.viewport: A numbered work index and mosaic mechanism share a rigid character grid.
options.risk: Retro broadcasting obscures the modern inventor character.
options.case: Loses audience identification through nostalgia and product clarity through coded navigation.
options.kept: Direct access to every work entry.

options.label: Engineering Specimen
options.thesis: A live variable-type specimen lets visitors reshape the engineering disciplines and reveal their project entries.
options.viewport: Huge discipline words and one axis slider dominate a tightly arranged project index.
options.risk: Typography, not engineering work, becomes the main artifact.
options.case: Loses audience identification to a type-foundry idiom and product clarity by making lettering the demonstration.
options.kept: One interaction coherently affects the complete illustration.

options.label: Instructions into Matter
options.thesis: Punched instructions and a woven result illustrate the passage from computation to physical action.
options.viewport: A woven illustrative mechanism aligns with its binary instruction matrix and project index.
options.risk: A textile practice is implied where none has been confirmed.
options.case: Loses audience identification through textile luxury and clarity through an unrelated fabrication medium.
options.kept: Traceability between a project overview and its supporting evidence.

options.label: Material Experiments
options.thesis: Engineering studies are explored as a sequence of material transformations in a firing log.
options.viewport: A large experimental material sample sits beside deliberate process-stage controls.
options.risk: Ceramics could be mistaken for the portfolio’s actual discipline.
options.case: Loses identification with robotics and clarity about what the owner actually builds.
options.kept: Convincing material variation in the illustrative object.

options.label: Inventor Episodes
options.thesis: Each engineering project becomes a boldly illustrated episode in an inventor’s ongoing series.
options.viewport: A project title and illustrative mechanism fill a single vivid animated title card.
options.case: Loses audience identification through cartoon nostalgia and clarity by presenting projects as entertainment episodes.
options.kept: A single focal object owns the opening at full scale.

options.label: Engineering Plate Book
options.thesis: A constructed alphabet and interlocking units organize projects as an assembly of research plates.
options.viewport: A large assembled geometric field connects illustrated project plates and their captions.
options.risk: Regional ornament suggests a cultural identity the owner has not claimed.
options.case: Loses audience identification through unrelated heritage and clarity through decorative abstraction.
options.kept: One structural grammar extends across homepage and future case studies.

canonCard.label: Straightforward portfolio
canonCard.thesis: An introduction, selected-work grid, about section, and T labs story in a familiar layout.
canonCard.viewport: A conventional introductory headline leads into a grid of project previews.
canonCard.risk: Easy to understand, but less distinctive.
